name: Qt
summary: A cross-platform application framework that combines QObject ownership and meta-object communication with event dispatch, widget hierarchies, and platform integration plugins.

features.name: QObject parent ownership tree
features.description: QObject accepts an optional parent and maintains child objects. Qt documents that deleting a parent deletes its children and that child objects are removed from the parent's child list when destroyed, giving many framework objects an explicit ownership tree.
benefits: Makes common object lifetime relationships explicit
Provides automatic cleanup for parented objects
costs: Ownership must match object lifetimes and thread rules
Parent-child ownership is not a universal substitute for value or shared ownership

features.name: Meta-object signal and slot communication
features.description: Qt's meta-object system registers signals, slots, properties, and invokable methods. Signals and slots connect publishers and receivers, with queued connections delivering calls through the receiver thread's event loop when sender and receiver live in different threads.
benefits: Supports synchronous and queued delivery through one connection abstraction
costs: Connection type and thread affinity affect ordering and execution context
Generated or runtime meta-object metadata increases framework complexity

features.name: Thread-affine event dispatch
features.description: QCoreApplication and QAbstractEventDispatcher provide the application event loop and per-thread event dispatch. QObject thread affinity determines where queued signals and posted events are delivered, while event filters and handlers participate in dispatch.
benefits: Unifies timers, posted events, input, and queued calls under dispatch loops
Makes execution context part of object behavior
costs: Blocking or absent event loops delay queued work
Thread affinity constrains object movement and cross-thread access

features.name: Widget and platform plugin boundary
features.description: Qt Widgets builds hierarchical QWidget objects while QPA exposes QPlatformIntegration and related interfaces for windowing, screens, themes, input, and native services. Platform plugins implement the backend-specific portion behind Qt GUI APIs.
benefits: Provides a common widget and GUI API across platform backends
Keeps platform integration replaceable and inspectable
costs: Backend capabilities and style behavior vary by platform plugin
Widget hierarchies and repaint/layout work create lifecycle and performance obligations

mathematical_views.model: Owned object forest with thread labels
mathematical_views.question: How do QObject parent-child edges and thread affinity determine lifetime and dispatch relationships?
assumptions: QObject instances are nodes and parent-child links are ownership edges
Each object has a thread-affinity label
The model abstracts C++ destruction details and shared-pointer exceptions

mathematical_views.question: How does a signal emission become direct or queued slot execution?
assumptions: Connections are typed or runtime-resolved edges between meta-objects
Connection type and thread affinity select a delivery transition
The model abstracts generated meta-object implementation

mathematical_views.question: Which widget and GUI operations are refined by a selected QPA platform plugin?
assumptions: Qt GUI calls are abstract operations
Platform plugin interfaces provide backend implementations
Capability and rendering equivalence must be checked per platform

benefits: Automatic cleanup follows explicit ownership edges
costs: Parenting and destruction order constrain composition

benefits: Loose coupling across object and thread boundaries
costs: Delivery semantics and metadata add runtime reasoning cost

benefits: A common loop handles timers, events, and queued calls
costs: Thread affinity and event-loop availability constrain responsiveness

benefits: Portable widgets over replaceable native backends
